delivery_slices.name: Outcome Fixture Corpus And Backtest Baseline
Release, Demo, And Product Signals Part 1
Release, Demo, And Product Signals Part 2

criteria: Memory writes must originate from verified outcome events. Agent self-reports and reflections must not enter memory in the MVP.
groups.title: FR1: Outcomes As The Only Memory Source

criteria: The MVP must work without a hosted Relia account. Memory lives in the repository.
groups.title: FR2: Repo-Native Local-First Operation

criteria: Relia must ingest PR metadata, check runs, reverts, and marked review corrections.
groups.title: FR3: GitHub Outcome Intake

criteria: Relia must attribute agent authorship via bot login, co-author trailer, and PR label, with method and confidence recorded. Uncertain attribution must fail closed (excluded from ERR) by default.
groups.title: FR4: Attribution With Confidence

criteria: Backtest, distill, serve, assess, and reports must consume canonical experience records.
groups.title: FR5: Canonical Experience Schema

criteria: Secrets must be redacted before experience records, reports, memory pages, compiled blocks, or shares are persisted.
groups.title: FR6: Capture-Time Redaction

criteria: Signature extraction must prefer structured check-run data and label log-parsed signatures with extraction confidence.
groups.title: FR7: Deterministic Failure Signatures

criteria: Relia must pair recurrences conservatively, separate `confirmed` from `possible`, and exclude `possible` from headline ERR.
groups.title: FR8: Conservative Recurrence Pairing

criteria: relia backtest` must deliver the ERR headline and paired evidence read-only, with no rules, review, or workflow change required.
groups.title: FR9: Backtest Before Behavior Change

criteria: Every rule must cite at least one experience and one PR. Uncited rules fail validation and never render.
groups.title: FR10: Provenance-Mandatory Rules

criteria: Confidence must derive from evidence count, recency, contradictions, flake discounts, and extraction confidence — never from the drafting model.
groups.title: FR11: Calibrated Confidence

criteria: Rules must decay by half-life and go `stale` when their scoped paths are deleted.
groups.title: FR12: Decay And Churn Invalidation

criteria: Drafted rules must be reviewed before becoming `active`, with `accepted`, `suggested`, and `needs_user_input` labels. Disabling review is an explicit, surfaced configuration choice.
groups.title: FR13: Human Review Gate

criteria: Relia must support `avoid` rules from failures and `playbook` rules from held fixes, and playbook rules must cite held evidence.
groups.title: FR14: Bidirectional Memory

criteria: relia memory` must render MEMORY.md showing statements, confidence, lifecycle status, and clickable provenance.
groups.title: FR15: Memory Page With Receipts

criteria: relia serve` must expose `recall`, `assess`, and `coverage` over MCP, serving only `active` rules.
groups.title: FR16: MCP Serving

criteria: relia compile` must maintain a managed, marker-delimited block in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, regenerable and never touching content outside the markers.
groups.title: FR17: Compiled Context Block

criteria: relia assess`, the MCP `assess` tool, and the PR comment must share one engine and one `RiskAssessment` schema.
groups.title: FR18: Advisory Assessment

criteria: Relia must report experience density for touched paths and label `no_coverage` distinctly from `covered_clean`.
groups.title: FR19: Coverage / OOD Signal

criteria: The GitHub Action must never block merges by default. The recurrence gate requires explicit configuration and exits `5` when tripped.
groups.title: FR20: Advisory-Only Default

criteria: Relia must track ERR against a saved baseline and label stale baselines.
groups.title: FR21: Forward ERR Tracking

criteria: Relia must support stable exit codes and `--json`.
groups.title: FR22: Stable CLI Output

criteria: Distillation must support OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic adapters behind a pluggable interface, BYO key, cost caps, and a deterministic no-LLM mode.
groups.title: FR23: Provider Adapters And No-LLM Mode

criteria: Distill runs using a provider must report token and estimated cost information.
groups.title: FR24: Cost Visibility

criteria: Experience records, rules, memory pages, reports, and baselines must remain useful outside any hosted service.
groups.title: FR25: Portable Artifacts

criteria: A technical user should run `relia demo` and open the bundled backtest report in under 5 minutes, and run a real `backtest` in under 10 minutes from install.
groups.title: NFR1: Fast First Value

criteria: A technical user should ingest, distill, and approve their first rule in under 30 minutes.
groups.title: NFR2: Fast First Memory

criteria: Repeated backtests over the same window and artifacts must produce the same result.
groups.title: NFR3: Deterministic Backtest

criteria: Reports must clearly distinguish confirmed recurrences, possible recurrences, flake-discounted evidence, and uncertain attribution.
groups.title: NFR4: Calibration Honesty

criteria: Redaction must happen before artifact persistence. If a value cannot be confidently redacted, Relia must fail closed (exit 6): mark the artifact unsafe to persist rather than write a possibly-unredacted secret. Silent persistence of an unrecognized secret is a trust bug, not an edge case.
groups.title: NFR5: Security

criteria: Relia must not send code, diffs, logs, or experience records anywhere by default. When a distill provider is configured, only redacted experience records leave the machine, and `relia check` must say so explicitly.
groups.title: NFR6: Local Privacy

criteria: Rule YAML and MEMORY.md must be understandable by engineers without a custom UI.
groups.title: NFR7: Rule Readability

criteria: Outcome extraction should use the GitHub API's structured data (check runs, review threads, merge/revert metadata) before log scraping; log-parsed values carry confidence labels.
groups.title: NFR8: Structured-Data-First

criteria: Errors must include file, path, PR, command, object, or line references where possible.
groups.title: NFR9: Debuggable Errors

criteria: Provider-backed distillation must show token and estimated cost information and respect `max_cost_usd_per_run`.
groups.title: NFR10: Cost Visibility

criteria: LLM-drafted statements are labeled by origin and reviewable; clustering and calibration are deterministic given the same inputs.
groups.title: NFR11: Stochastic Honesty

criteria: Schemas and artifacts must be versioned.
groups.title: NFR12: Artifact Stability

criteria: Drafted rules, signatures parsed from logs, attribution inferences, and held-fix detection must be confidence-labeled.
groups.title: NFR13: Inference Humility

criteria: The PR advisor must default to at most one comment per PR and edit that comment in place on subsequent pushes rather than posting new ones. Reassessment is debounced (default 10 minutes) and skipped entirely when the diff fingerprint is unchanged, so force-push storms produce one living comment, not a thread. The advisor stays silent below `min_confidence` and on `covered_clean`.
groups.title: NFR14: Advisory Restraint

criteria: The MVP must explain value through local CLI output, local reports, MEMORY.md, and the PR comment.
groups.title: NFR15: No Dashboard Dependency

groups.title: MVP In Scope

criteria: The MVP is not complete until all acceptance groups pass.
groups.title: Acceptance Tests

criteria: relia init` writes valid config with discovered checks and candidate attribution markers.
relia check` flags zero-match attribution config with a concrete reference.
relia ingest` writes schema-valid, redacted experience records for PRs, check runs, reverts, and marked corrections.
Attribution records method and confidence; an ambiguous trailer yields `attribution_uncertain` and exclusion from ERR.
relia backtest --window 180d` is deterministic on repeated runs.
Confirmed recurrences are paired with the earlier experience they repeat, with resolvable links.
Possible recurrences appear separately and are excluded from headline ERR.
The planted flaky test is discounted and drafts no rule.
Seeded secrets never appear in any artifact.
relia demo` opens the bundled backtest and memory-page reports with no install, token, model key, or hosted account.
Attribution precision is at least 95% on a labeled sample; uncertain cases are excluded, not guessed.
groups.title: Ingest, Attribute, Backtest Acceptance Tests

criteria: relia distill` drafts an `avoid` rule from the planted recurrence cluster with correct citations.
relia distill` drafts a `playbook` rule citing the held fix.
A rule without provenance fails `relia check` with exit 4.
Drafted rules are `suggested` or `needs_user_input`, never auto-`accepted`.
relia review` approve/edit/reject transitions write correct lifecycle states.
The planted contradiction moves its rule to `contradicted` and out of serving.
The planted path deletion moves its rule to `stale` and out of serving.
MEMORY.md renders receipts as resolvable links and separates weak from strong memory.
No-LLM mode produces deterministic cluster-summary drafts.
Provider-backed distill reports cost and respects the configured cap.
relia models pull records model ID, version, source URL, license, digest, cache path, update policy, and rollback policy before local embedding refinement is used.

embeddings: local fails closed with exit 8 when the local model artifact is missing, stale, or digest-mismatched, while embeddings: signature remains the zero-install deterministic fallback with signature-only provenance.
Release binaries, containers, and tracked source do not bundle model weights or inference-runtime payloads.
The local embedding inference boundary is covered by an ADR before implementation chooses a pure Go library, ONNX/runtime binding, or external local process.
groups.title: Distill, Review, Memory Page Acceptance Tests

criteria: relia serve` exposes `recall`, `assess`, and `coverage` over MCP and serves only `active` rules.
A real agent session retrieves a rule via `recall` and the rule's citations resolve.
relia compile` maintains the managed block idempotently and never edits outside markers.
relia assess` returns `match_high` with citations on a planted-pattern diff and `no_coverage` on unknown paths.
The GitHub Action posts at most one advisory comment per PR, citing real PRs.
The Action stays silent below `min_confidence` and on `covered_clean`.
The Action never blocks by default; with the gate explicitly enabled, a tripped threshold exits 5.
ERR trend compares against the saved baseline and labels staleness.
relia share` re-runs redaction at export, produces a single self-contained artifact, and fails closed when unsafe.
The README badge reflects current ERR and reads as stale after 30 days without ingest or 20 merged PRs since the last ingest, whichever comes first.
groups.title: Serve And Advise Acceptance Tests

criteria: bundled demo report opened in under 5 minutes
first real backtest completed in under 10 minutes from install
first rule distilled, reviewed, and active in under 30 minutes
backtest finds a nonzero recurrence story on the user's own repo
user runs `ingest` more than once (incremental usage)
user installs the GitHub Action
agent sessions query the MCP server in real work
user edits or adds rules by hand (ownership signal)
user adds a second repository
user cites the memory page or backtest report in a team discussion or PR
at least 70% of confirmed recurrence pairs judged correct on human spot-check
at least 60% of `suggested` drafts accepted without edit
100% of served rules carry resolvable citations
advisory comment precision at least 70% on spot-check ("was this warning relevant?")
no unredacted secrets in standard Relia artifacts
headline ERR never includes possible recurrences or uncertain attribution
groups.title: Success Metrics

criteria: relia demo` works offline with no configuration.
Every number shown live is reproducible from the seeded repo.
The memory-off/memory-on contrast uses the same task, model, and prompt.
Every citation shown in the demo resolves to a real PR in the seeded repo.
The fallback static reports cover all five beats.
groups.title: Demo Acceptance
Agent-Native CLI Conventions
criteria: Agent-facing CLI output supports stable JSON mode or records an approved deferral.
Non-interactive or piped output is machine-readable unless the command is explicitly human-only.
Quiet and compact modes preserve status, evidence refs, typed exits, and machine-readable errors.
